He takes the waitress's wrist with the same economy he used on the clerk and the nurse, and he stops while she can still stand and lock her knees. Color leaves her face. His hunger falls. He writes nothing yet. He leaves a plate already clean.

Outside the register light he writes three names and three regeneration windows in the map margin, a clean rotation locked. Paying, tipping, and steadying the clerk were method. The margin now holds a hardware clerk, a night nurse, and a graveyard-shift waitress.

Before first light Hale spreads the marked map on a closed shop window. He has left the diner. Church bulletins, a hardware circular, and the names of civic stones are laid against the streets he already walked.

He writes the word ritual once, then the count of tokens, then the stone in the old green. He folds the map so that column faces in. Hunger has come back into his hands. He puts them in his pockets and walks on.

The clerk, the nurse, and the waitress have their color back. Hale's own hunger has climbed through the hours of walking the long way around the lights. He reads each rewrite as weather and does not change his route except to avoid the tubes.

Hale takes the waitress's wrist a third time at the empty end of the counter and stops, as before, while she can still lock her knees. He has come in from the street. He does not sit for a plate this time. He leaves her standing.

He counts remaining cash and remaining hours against a clerk, a nurse, and a waitress none of whom will receive him. He crosses the last unlit service lane already shaking. Hunger climbs past the point where the map still feels like control. Unfed, Cora's color comes back.

gr-03.beat_text: On the college lawn a ring of students pass a cup and do not flinch at teeth. The group stands in the open as willing donors. Fourteen of them are already organized. Hale sees the ring from the long way around and does not enter the quad.

gr-04.beat_text: Hospital coolers that held bags yesterday hold ice and a handwritten tribute list. Night access is badge only. The wards that were an open ledger are now a squeezed one. Tribute-or-starve is in force for anyone who still needs hospital blood.

cn-01.beat_text: He isolates a finite set of objects that must already exist in town and one dawn invocation that can be spoken at only one site. The prize is the only paying door left. The road has already looped him once. He treats the count as solvable.

Completing the invocation at first light would end the match. An ended match is a wipe with no morning after for any stack of photographs. He looks from the tokens to the print of the stone taken on a night that would vanish with the win.

cn-02.beat_text: She lines the prints on the prep table and does not clock in on time. A seam of roll-bar crawls the break-room TV and holds. Sleep did not take the night. The failsafe that should have erased her has a visible seam.

She keeps the recorder running under the counter through the dinner prep. Denise leaves without finishing her coffee and does not look at the door. The leak in the wipe is no longer a private seam. Cora's hands shake once on the clip, then still.

The extra write does not shut anything. More Hosts wake with scraps. A man at the bus stop describes last night to a woman who should not remember him. Fragments walk the block. The clerk touches his own neck and keeps the hour.

cn-03.beat_text: She is testing whether a modeled mind will carry a lie across a sleep. She does not know the three names already sit in another Guest's margin. She notes the baseline in a pocket book and walks back toward the college before any of the three lie down.

cn-04.beat_text: He does not take the tape. His hand stays on the table, fingers aligned with the Formica grain. The repeating figure now has a name she can keep. Something in her face goes flat at the sound of herself being emptied on command.

Anja closes the pocket book without a new baseline and walks faster than the hunger in her own throat. Cora stands unblinking in the aftershock of the extra write, the night piling up with no place to put it. The town is now too awake.
